newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq in favor of renewal of oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq in favor of renewal of oil-for-food deal.

text.p: Iraq's ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said his country was in favor of renewing the oil-for-food deal that expires early next month, the United Nations reported on Friday.

But U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Hamdoon, in a meeting with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, complained about the passivity of the international community in speaking out against Turkish incursions in the north of Iraq.

Eckhard also said that Annan would present a report on the oil-for-food plan to the Security Council on Monday, which is due to make a decision on its renewal before June 9. The council's sanctions committee is expected to present its own report on the resolution at the same time.

The oil-for-food deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to provide needed humanitarian supplies for civilians suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed in August 1990. It went into effect on December 10.

Eckhard said Hamdoon had told Annan his "government favored renewal." He also said that while he was pleased with Annan's previous statements on the Turkey's actions, his government was "concerned about the silence and passivity of the international community as a whole. "
